## Phase 1 Task ID

State the canonical task identifier exactly as it appears in the Phase 1 plan set, for example `P1-01-DO-002`. One issue represents one task. If the identifier is not yet allocated, state that explicitly rather than inventing one.

## Objective

State, in one or two complete sentences, what this task is intended to achieve. Describe the outcome, not the activity. Do not restate the task title.

## Scope

### In scope

List the specific deliverables, files, modules, or decisions this task covers.

-
-

### Out of scope

List work that is deliberately excluded, including anything deferred to a later phase or to a future workstream.

-
-

## Dependencies

List the task identifiers, decisions, approvals, or environment conditions that must exist before this task can proceed. Record each dependency with its current status.

| Dependency | Type                                     | Status                     |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
|            | Task / Decision / Approval / Environment | Open / Satisfied / Blocked |

If a dependency is blocked or unavailable, record it as Blocked. Do not describe a blocked dependency as satisfied.

## Definition of Ready

Confirm each condition before work starts. Leave a box unticked where the condition is not met, and note the reason.

- [ ] The task identifier is confirmed against the Phase 1 plan set.
- [ ] The objective and scope are unambiguous and agreed.
- [ ] All dependencies are either satisfied or explicitly recorded as Blocked.
- [ ] The owner role is assigned.
- [ ] The acceptance condition is stated and is objectively testable.
- [ ] The evidence required is identified and can be produced.

## Definition of Done

Confirm each condition before the issue is closed.

- [ ] Every in-scope deliverable is produced.
- [ ] The acceptance condition is met and demonstrated by the recorded evidence.
- [ ] The evidence is attached to, or linked from, this issue.
- [ ] Any residual gap, risk, or blocked item is recorded openly rather than omitted.
- [ ] Statements made in the deliverable are factual and measured; no test result, approval, environment, or compliance claim is asserted without evidence.
- [ ] Changes are committed on the correct working branch and the branch is stated in this issue.

## Acceptance condition

State the single condition that determines whether this task passes. It must be verifiable by a party other than the author, and it must be expressed so that the outcome is either met or not met. Avoid subjective wording.

## Evidence required

Specify the artefacts that will demonstrate the acceptance condition, and where each will be located.

| Evidence artefact | Form                                                                | Location |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
|                   | Command output / File / Screenshot / Register entry / Reviewer note |          |

Record measured values rather than expected values. Where a command was executed, record the command and its actual output. Where an item could not be verified, record it as Not verified and state why.

## Owner role

State the role accountable for the task and the role that verifies it.

- Accountable role:
- Verifying role:

Where the verifying role is the same person as the accountable role, state this explicitly and record it as an independence gap.

## Notes

Record any additional context, constraints, or open questions. Do not record credentials, tokens, keys, or any other secret material in this issue.
